transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-23 17:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min | Attendees: Alex, Priya, Ethan (Redwood) — Sara, Miguel, Jenna, Tom (Acme)

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync to review perf bench vs baseline provider; root causes of jitter; next steps to run quantized / dedicated tests.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda — run through this week's benchmark, highlight deltas vs your baseline, then ops/tuning recommendations and next steps.
[00:18] Sara (Acme): yeah thanks Alex, we ran your tests last night, we've got the logs, Miguel will share network and infra details, just keen to see the p95 numbers — our baseline's been pretty inconsistent.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): cool. Quick note on methodology: we ran the same model checkpoint, same prompt corpus you provided, synthetic concurrency patterns to match peak-hour traffic — we tested hosted Redwood, plus a Dedicated quick-run on an A100 pool, and compared to your baseline provider (you called them "Vecro" during onboarding, which maps to their managed endpoint on Vertex). There may be some naming mismatches in the transcript.
[01:05] Ethan (Redwood Eng): for clarity: tests used seq len 512, batch sizes [1,4,8], caching on/off. Metrics captured: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and end-to-end throughput req/s. We also captured CPU egress times to catch network variance.
[01:40] Miguel (Acme SRE): our baseline numbers — p95 around 620ms for single-token streaming requests during your baseline run, throughput ~220 req/s at batch 1 under our infra. We saw spikes to ~850ms at peak.
[02:05] Priya: thanks, in Redwood hosted runs we saw p95 ~420ms for same workload, p50 ~110ms, and throughput ~350 req/s (batch=1). With batch=8 and quantization enabled we pushed tokens/sec up, throughput peaked around 900 tokens/sec.
[02:40] Jenna (Product): those are promising. Can you explain where most of the delta came from? is it kernel selection, batching, or network?
[02:55] Priya: it's a combination; primary wins were smarter kernel selection and continuous batching in the serving runtime, plus our prefix/K V cache auto-warm (sorry K V written out in notes). Baseline was not using aggressive batching and their kv cache invalidated more often. Also we observed about 8-12% improvement on H100 vs A100 in our internal runs which the baseline wasn't using.
[03:30] Tom (CTO): any differences in token quality or output variance when you quantized? that's a concern for our product quality metrics.
[03:45] Ethan: good Q — we did int4 quant runs on a copy and saw negligible quality delta on the eval set you provided (ROUGE/semantic checks), but there are edge cases; Priya will run targeted prompts with your failure cases next.
[04:10] Alex: I'll call out cost side briefly — rough unit economics: during tests Redwood hosted effective cost per 1k tokens was about $0.80 vs baseline ~ $1.20 (these are illustrative, final pricing will vary by committed capacity and exact model).
[04:35] Sara: can you confirm total cost savings estimate for our expected monthly traffic (we put in ~3B tokens/month)?
[04:50] Alex: ballpark that would be ~20-25% savings with hosted; larger if you move to Dedicated with reserved capacity and optimized quantization. We'll send a modelled spreadsheet.
[05:12] Miguel: network wise, we noticed about 30ms egress to your hosted region from our cluster which we accounted for; curious if dedicated in-region helps.
[05:30] Priya: yes dedicated/cloud proximity helps — for Dedicated you can choose region-level placement; in the dedicated tests we saw p95 drop another ~40-60ms when colocated. We'll demo that if you want.
[06:05] Jenna: what about security/compliance basics — SSO, audit logs, KMS? We need SOC2 for procurement.
[06:20] Alex: Redwood has SOC2 and supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; we'll attach the security pack after the call.
[06:35] Sara: thanks. Back to perf: were these numbers stable across runs? we saw jitter.
[06:45] Ethan: variance exists. Our runs show STDDEV on p95 around 30-40ms across 10 runs for hosted; your baseline had higher variance — matching your spikes. We dug into GC/eviction on their side. Could be model cache thrash.
[07:10] Miguel: interesting — do you have the eviction metrics and the eviction window params?
[07:20] Priya: yes we log cache hit rates and eviction counts; in our test hit rate was ~92% with prefix caching, baseline was ~78%. We'll include the raw hit-rate CSV.
[07:40] Sara: curious about real-time streaming latencies — our product uses chunked streaming; how did that compare?
[07:55] Priya: streaming tail p95 was similar to request p95 results; though baseline had a higher tail due to irregular batching and higher TTFB on first token. Redwood's fast kernel path reduces first-token time in many cases.
[08:20] Tom: any infra caveats? e.g., if we go into production with reserved capacity do you throttle or change queueing?
[08:30] Alex: reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and isolation; there are autoscale policies but we can set burst allowances. We'll capture recommended autoscale policy for your traffic profile.
[09:00] Jenna: can you share the exact test commands and configs you used? we want to reproduce.
[09:10] Priya: yes — we'll push a runbook with the exact curl/SDK commands, model config (quant/precision), and the env variables (KV cache TTLs, batch windows).
[09:30] Miguel: about hardware: you mentioned H100 gains; were those from quant runs or any special kernel tuning?
[09:45] Ethan: H100 had better matrix throughput; combined with fused attention kernels we saw improvements, but quantization is orthogonal. Kernel selection was automated by the runtime based on seq len and model shape. Some naming got fuzzy in logs — sometimes we saw model labelled as "rwv2" in spots — ignore that, it's internal shorthand.
[10:20] Sara: regarding benchmarking fairness — did you warm the model equally for both providers? sometimes warm vs cold causes huge diffs.
[10:30] Priya: good point — we did both cold and warm runs. The comparative numbers I quoted were warm runs after steady-state for 10 minutes. Cold starts for baseline were worse (p95 up to 1.2s) while Redwood cold start p95 ~700ms.
[11:00] Alex: wanted to highlight a specific test: at 200 concurrent users simulating product traffic, baseline throughput fell off at 180 req/s while Redwood stayed linear to ~340 req/s. That's due to our continuous batching and request coalescing.
[11:25] Miguel: are there logs showing queue lengths? that will help SRE to tune ingress.
[11:35] Ethan: included in the CSV we will send — queue depth, batch size distribution, kernel selection per request.
[12:05] Jenna: any risks with quantizing for our generation tasks? we have long-tail completion prompts.
[12:20] Priya: risk exists for some long-context generative tasks; we'll run your flagged prompts next cycle. If quality differs we'll recommend hybrid: quantize where safe and fallback to higher precision for flagged prompts.
[12:50] Sara: sounds reasonable. On timelines — if we see a 20% cost savings and p95 <500ms we'd be willing to pilot dedicated.
[13:05] Alex: noted. We'll aim to show that in next week's run.
[13:20] Priya: next test items: run batch=8 quant on Dedicated A100/H100 variants, and run warm/cold tests with streaming enabled.
[13:40] Miguel: also want to replicate the baseline run parameters — I will send the exact script used by baseline by EOD.
[14:00] Ethan: great — when we get that we can run an apples-to-apples.
[14:15] Alex: any procurement blockers? Jenna?
[14:25] Jenna: just security pack and cost modeling; procurement will sign if pilot meets SLA and compliance checklist. We'll need sample SLA language.
[14:35] Alex: will attach standard SLA language and SOC2 docs.
[15:00] Sara: one more question — you mentioned fallback policies if capacity constrained. How does that affect latency?
[15:10] Priya: we have automatic fallback to smaller/compatible model variants; the runtime routes by policy. Fallback may increase hallucination risk vs latency but keeps app online; we'll share recommended fallback chain.
[15:40] Miguel: OK. can you also surface the edge case where batching increases latency for single-user interactive flows?
[15:55] Priya: yes, we can tune min_batch_delay so interactive p50 stays low while still getting batching benefits. We'll provide knobs.
[16:20] Tom: fine. let's recap next steps.
[16:30] Alex: recap — Alex send benchmark csv + charts; Priya do quant/dedicated runs; Ethan include runbook and raw logs; Miguel send baseline script; Sara confirm success criteria. We'll reconvene same time next week unless earlier required.
[16:50] Sara: thanks all. Appreciate the deep dive.
[16:57] Alex: thanks team, I'll follow up with sheet + security pack.

End of transcript.
